title: Introduce modular CI shims and staged-lint resume flow to reduce presubmit latency
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added modular CI helper modules and a staged-lint resume mechanism to improve presubmit feedback latency and reduce wasted lint runs. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit pipeline spends a lot of time reinitializing lint tooling for small edits and re-running the full lint graph after transient failures. This PR splits CI helper logic into small go modules (ci/shim modules) and introduces a staged-lint resume mechanism so that lint shards can resume from the last successful checkpoint instead of restarting fully.

Summary of changes (single-line sections kept inside one string):
- Extract ci helpers: move common GH Action entrypoint logic into lightweight Go modules under infra/ci/shims. These expose a small CLI that runs setup, priming, and checksum validation so composite actions can be trimmed.
- Staged-lint resume: add a resume token mechanism for lint shards. Each lint job writes a checkpoint artifact (lint-checkpoint-{shard}.json) containing the set of files it validated and the linter versions used. On re-run, the lint runner will compare the resume token and skip shards that have an exact checkpoint match.
- Runtime optimizations: add a sparse filewatcher to fast-detect changed packages and only invoke per-language linters for impacted workspaces.
- CI composition: replace a few monolithic composite actions with thin wrappers that call the go shims; this reduces action YAML complexity and action startup overhead.
- Observability: emit a small telemetry event (ci.shim.start / ci.lint.resume_hit) to our internal CI metrics pipeline for future SLO calculations. Events are opt-out via CI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY.

Checklist (what I did):
- [x] Extracted helper logic into infra/ci/shims/go modules and published go.mod entries
- [x] Implemented resume token creation and validation in lint runner
- [x] Updated GitHub Actions to call the shims instead of embedding logic in YAML
- [x] Added unit tests for checksum/resume logic and small integration test for resume flow
- [x] Ran staged pipeline on canary repos for 48 hours and validated average presubmit latency down 28% on small pushes

Commits (high-level):
- 7aa2b1c: infra/ci/shims: initial go module, basic entrypoint and config parsing
- f3b4d6e: lint/runner: add checkpoint serialization and resume token compare
- d2c1e8a: actions: replace composite linter with shim invocation and upload/download checkpoint artifacts
- 9b8f0a2: tests: add unit tests for checksum logic and CI integration smoke test

Files changed (high-level):
- infra/ci/shims/main.go (new) — lightweight CLI used by actions
- infra/ci/shims/checksum.go (new) — deterministic workspace fingerprinting
- tools/lint/runner.go (modified) — checkpoint write/compare and resume logic added
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yml (modified) — now calls shims and uses checkpoint artifacts
- .github/actions/lint-composite/action.yml (removed) — logic moved to shims
- scripts/ci_telemetry_wrapper.sh (modified) — small wrapper to gate telemetry env var
- tests/ci/lint_resume_test.go (new) — integration-level smoke test
- go.mod / go.sum (modified) — new module entries and pinned deps

How this was validated:
- Canary run: wired the branch into two small repos (redwood-examples and perf-canary) for 48h, measured presubmit median drop of 28% for edits that only touched single packages and resume-hit rate ~62% for repeated commits that retriggered CI within 10 minutes.
- Unit tests: checksum diffs and resume comparator covered edge cases (ordering, timestamp variance, transitive ignores).
- Manual review: ran a full lint-suite locally and verified output parity when resume is not applicable.

Review conversation (abridged inside the description string):
- Aisha Rahman: "Can the checkpoint artifact leak produced file contents? We need to ensure we never store secrets or paths with user data."
- Author (Maya): "Checkpoint only contains file list relative paths and linter version hashes. I added a sanitizer to drop absolute paths and excluded any generated directories (build/, dist/) — see checksum.go#sanitizePaths."
- Diego Marquez: "What happens if a linter binary is upgraded mid-rollout? Could false resume hits mask real regressions?"
- Author: "Resume token includes linter version hashes as reported by each language runner. On version mismatch we treat it as miss and rerun full shard. Added unit test for mismatch behavior."
- Samir Kulkarni: "CI telemetry env var default should be off in external CI runs."
- Author: "Default is off; we enable in our internal runners only. See scripts/ci_telemetry_wrapper.sh."

CI: initial run showed a flaky lint-test integration on the third job (timeout during vendor download). I re-ran the failing job; subsequent run passed and overall status is green. Checks summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-smoke: pass (after rerun), lint: pass, e2e-nightly: skipped for PR.

Merge decision & strategy: Squash-merged to main after approvals. Merge method: squash. Release notes were added to the PR description and the change is non-breaking for customers. Post-merge we triggered a lightweight rollout for presubmit runners (gradually enable in 10% of CI pools, monitor ci.lint.resume_hit and presubmit latency for regressions).

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Wire resume telemetry to the CI SLO dashboard and create a short alert if resume_hit drops below 40% (ENG-4302).
- Add a periodic background job to garbage collect stale checkpoint artifacts older than 7 days.
- Consider adding a per-language delta strategy (only re-run per-language linters when their file sets change) as a second phase.

Risk assessment: Low-medium. The correctness of resume logic is guarded by checksum + linter-version matching; worst case is a false negative skip (which would be caught by downstream longer-running CI when full lint runs are scheduled) but tests and canary runs indicate acceptable safety.

If anything in this PR needs reverting quickly, revert the .github/workflows change (it will fall back to the old composite action in the main branch until we remove the composite file).
